tasks.short: Develop medical research methods and present findings

steps.what: Design medical methodology and experimental validation
Conduct experiments and capture source observations in the laboratory notebook
Prepare and check the analysis dataset from source observations
Run specified statistical summaries and produce analysis figures
Interpret results, challenge assumptions and assess medical applicability
Write scientific and public presentation materials from checked findings
Check final materials for evidence, privacy and audience suitability
Present the findings and answer scientific or public questions

tasks.design: Reuse validated summary and plotting configurations in the {DATA_PLATFORM} after the scientist prepares the dataset from the laboratory-notebook category {OTHER}. Keep study design, experiments, interpretation, presentation writing and audience questions human; the final materials are checked before delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research datasets and assumptions differ enough that unvalidated analysis reuse can mislead.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned native analysis presets remove repeated plotting setup while preserving scientist review.
tasks.still_hard: Novel methodology, instrument limitations, causal interpretation and explaining uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a statistically tidy result does not support a medical claim.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less figure setup, with unchanged scientific responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: validated statistical and plotting presets can reduce repeated setup; they cannot validate a novel medical method or causal claim.

assumptions: Boundary covers one research-to-presentation cycle. Shares are hypotheses, not measured study effort; manuscript publication and grant applications are separate tasks.

The scientist creates the method in s1, captures experimental observations in s2b and prepares/checks sample identifiers, variables, units, exclusions and missing values in s3. No free structured dataset or automated extraction is assumed.

{OTHER} is the laboratory notebook. s2 is physical experiment work; s2b separately counts first notebook entry, fully retained with its ordinary ungated save. Existing notebook fields do not remove source observation entry in this boundary; dataset transformation is separately s3. Test native analysis presets before custom code. Only plot and summary setup, 25% of s4, is removed; numerical runtime already automatic has no labour saving.

Failed presets and novel analyses are handled manually within retained s4-s5. Ordinary notebook and material saves remain fully retained without self-gates. s7 binds final materials and intended audience before delivery; materially changed claims require fresh checking.
No clinical deployment or change to patient care is authorised by this presentation workflow.
research_questions: Which summary and figure configurations reproduce validated results without new data preparation?

already_counted.description: Dataset preparation, failed-preset repair, interpretation and final material checks remain.

incremental.description: Scientist checks analysis presets after library or method changes.

approvals.approved_version: s7 final presentation materials and intended scientific or public audience; changed claims void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 8*0.25=2 setup hours removed less 0.7 upkeep gives 1.3 net. Cautious case: a new assay needs bespoke plots, leaving 0.8 hours of reusable axis and export setup and 0.1 net; all experimental and interpretive work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach medical principles and laboratory procedures

steps.what: Select teaching objectives and verify current medical and laboratory guidance
Prepare lesson materials and laboratory demonstrations
Verify final lesson content and demonstration safety
Teach principles and procedures and supervise learner practice

tasks.design: Reuse native {DOCS} lesson headings and demonstration-checklist layout while the scientist writes and checks current medical content. Retain live explanation, safe demonstration and learner supervision in full.
tasks.previous_blocker: The lesson must fit learner competence and current procedures.
tasks.enabler_now: Document layout reuse removes a small repeated preparation action.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising misunderstanding and unsafe laboratory technique.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt explanations and intervene during practice.
tasks.altitude: Small preparation saving with unchanged teaching responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reusable lesson layouts remove formatting but do not replace medical content verification or supervised practice.

assumptions: Boundary is lesson preparation and in-person teaching, not a formal assessment or certification process. Provisional shares require observation.
The scientist selects source guidance and learner objectives in s1 and writes actual materials in s2. No transcript, automatic content generation or new structured capture is assumed.
Test native {DOCS} templates. Only headings and checklist layout, 8% of s2, are removed. Medical wording, demonstration setup, final checks and ordinary saving stay.

No separate handout send or training-completion register is established here. If learners actually receive a published copy or require a completion entry, count those first writes and releases rather than creating a new teaching log.
unknowns: Whether completion records or handout releases belong to this teaching assignment
research_questions: Does the reusable layout shorten preparation without obscuring procedure changes?

already_counted.description: Content preparation, safety checking and live teaching remain.

incremental.description: Scientist refreshes lesson layout after procedure or curriculum changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.08=1.6 layout hours removed less 0.4 upkeep gives 1.2 net. Cautious case: a new instrument requires a bespoke demonstration checklist, leaving 0.5 reusable-heading hours and 0.1 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and publish scientific journal articles

steps.what: Assemble verified study results, source references and author contributions
Write the manuscript from checked results and source references

loop.purpose: Draft source-grounded methods and results wording, leaving scientific argument to the scientist
loop.input: checked manuscript source pack and journal instructions
loop.check: Scientist verifies every factual claim, numbers, methods, negation, uncertainty and citation against originals; rewrites unsupported interpretation
loop.stop: Missing source support or two failed drafts means manual writing in this step
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native journal layout and reference fields first; variable scientific prose still needs source-grounded drafting and full meaning review

steps.what: Resolve scientific and coauthor revisions and finish publication checks
outputs: final manuscript and journal submission payload

steps.what: Submit the approved manuscript and declarations to the journal
inputs: final manuscript and journal submission payload

steps.what: Address peer review and proof corrections before publication
Send the final checked revision or proof response to the journal

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} journal formatting and reference fields first, then a bounded drafting loop for source-grounded methods and results wording. The scientist retains interpretation, every claim check, coauthor coordination and all journal interactions; submission and later revision release each follow their completed-version check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drafting consumes time, but plausible unsupported prose can damage the paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can reduce initial wording effort with full scientist review.
tasks.still_hard: Novel claims, causal inference, authorship agreement and answering peer review.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what the evidence supports and defend limitations honestly.
tasks.altitude: Some initial wording is shorter; scientific accountability and peer review stay.

evidence.claim: Benchling AI drafts notebook entries and study reports; this supports source-document drafting capability, not autonomous journal authorship or acceptance.

assumptions: Focal boundary spans writing, initial submission and the scientist's revision/proof cycle. Journal editorial labour and coauthors' separate labour are outside the denominator, and no saving of their work is claimed. Shares are provisional.

The scientist assembles verified tables, method versions, limitations, reference identifiers and contribution records in s1 from the laboratory-notebook category {OTHER}. No free PDF extraction or invented reference lookup is assumed; missing sources are manually resolved in s1-s3.
Only 15% of s2 is removed by first-draft wording; checking every claim, scientific argument and failed-draft repair remain within its 85%. No model writes peer-review evaluations.

This scientist is the authorised submitting author. s3 includes checking the complete submission, actual coauthor permissions, declarations and exact journal destination; absent permissions stop submission. If another person performs a required approval, add their actual actor step and time. s5 similarly checks the final revised package before s6; edits void the corresponding approval.
Ordinary author saves remain in writing steps, fully retained and ungated. Journal portal entry remains fully retained; no invented same-system save benefit.
unknowns: Actual author and journal submission permissions
Draft quality and repair effort on this research field
research_questions: Can source-linked drafting reduce wording effort while preserving uncertainty and every citation?

already_counted.description: Draft review and repair, final submission checks and revision/proof checks remain.

incremental.description: Scientist maintains source restrictions and checks drafting behaviour after model changes.

approvals.approved_version: s3 completed manuscript, declarations, author permissions and exact journal submission payload/destination; edits void approval
s5 final checked revision or proof response with exact journal destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 35*0.15=5.25 drafting hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 4.25 net. Cautious case: a novel method cannot reuse most draft wording, leaving 1.2 hours of straightforward results wording removed and 0.2 net; all source verification and peer-review response work stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read funder requirements and check eligibility, evidence and project constraints
Develop the scientific plan, methods, partnerships and requested resources
Write the application narrative and required sections
Check application claims, budget consistency and required fields

tasks.design: Configure the actual funder's section headings, word limits and required-field checklist in {DOCS}. The scientist develops and writes the research argument and checks the budget against the scientific plan; the task ends at the checked application, with institutional approval and submission as separate workflows.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each call needs a funder-specific structure and a convincing research plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can remove recreation of required sections without inventing the science.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, feasibility, resource justification and partner commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a research question and credible method that warrant funding.
tasks.altitude: Less application formatting; unchanged scientific and budget responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: funder-specific document templates can carry required headings and word limits while the scientist retains substantive application writing.

assumptions: Boundary is writing the application, as stated, and ends at the checked package. No application send is hidden in writing or claimed as a saving. Institutional approval and submission must be separately mapped if included later. Shares are hypotheses.

The funder supplies current call, section requirements, word limits and eligibility rules; the scientist reads and manually verifies them in s1. The scientist produces scientific decisions in s2 from actual evidence and partner commitments, with no free structured narrative.
Test native {DOCS} templates first. Only recreation of required headings and word-limit layout, 10% of s3, is removed. All argument, method writing, checking and ordinary saving remain.
No generative drafting or grant-assessor automation is proposed. National and funder rules must be checked for the actual application.
unknowns: Actual institutional approvals and submission ownership
How much formatting the funder portal already supplies
research_questions: Does a call-specific template remove work beyond the funder's existing form?

already_counted.description: Application research decisions, substantive writing and final verification remain.

incremental.description: Scientist refreshes call-specific template and limits for each new funder version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25*0.10=2.5 layout hours removed less 0.7 upkeep gives 1.8 net. Cautious case: the call uses a new portal with bespoke sections, leaving only 0.8 hours of reusable required-field layout and 0.1 net; scientific writing remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Validated analysis setup and limited document assistance shorten supporting work while scientific design, interpretation and communication remain accountable human work.
skills_to_grow: Bind publication approval to a complete version and destination
role.ambitious_version: No expanded clinical authority or autonomous publication is justified.
